source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 4 (Distribution of Oceans and Continents).

sections.heading: 1. Continental Drift Theory
points: **Alfred Wegener (1912)** proposed **Continental Drift** — all continents were once a single landmass called **Pangaea**, surrounded by a single ocean **Panthalassa**.
Pangaea split into **Laurasia (north)** and **Gondwanaland (south)**, separated by the **Tethys Sea**.

sub: **Jigsaw fit** of continents (e.g. South America and Africa).
Matching **rocks, fossils** (Glossopteris, Mesosaurus), **tillite** deposits, **placer** deposits, coal seams across continents.

points: Wegener's proposed forces (tidal, buoyancy) were considered inadequate — the theory was later refined.

sections.heading: 2. Sea-Floor Spreading
points: **Harry Hess** proposed **sea-floor spreading**: new oceanic crust forms at **mid-oceanic ridges** where magma rises, and spreads outward.
Evidence: **paleomagnetism** (magnetic stripes of alternating polarity, symmetrical about ridges), young rocks near ridges, older away.
Ocean floor is **destroyed at trenches (subduction)** — so the Earth is not expanding.

sections.heading: 3. Plate Tectonics
points: The lithosphere is broken into **plates** that move over the asthenosphere (driven by **convection currents**).
**Seven major** and several minor plates (Indian, Pacific, African, Eurasian, etc.).

sub: **Divergent (constructive)** — plates move apart (mid-ocean ridges); new crust forms.
**Convergent (destructive)** — plates collide; subduction, mountains (Himalayas), trenches, volcanoes.
**Transform (conservative)** — plates slide past (e.g. San Andreas Fault).

points: The **Himalayas** formed by the collision of the **Indian and Eurasian plates**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Continental Drift = Wegener (1912); Pangaea + Panthalassa; split into Laurasia + Gondwana (Tethys between).
Sea-floor spreading = Harry Hess; magma rises at mid-ocean ridges.
Paleomagnetic stripes = proof of sea-floor spreading.
Three plate boundaries: divergent, convergent, transform.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Convergent boundaries** cause mountains/subduction; **divergent** create new crust.
The **San Andreas Fault** is a **transform** boundary.
